observer_bug.summary: the canonical-state spy keyed its reference tensors by Python id(obj)
observer_bug.detail: canonical_path_proofs stores the raw K / V appended to every CanonicalLayerState in a dict keyed by id(self). It first runs core.score(model, ctx, cont, 'rabit') (3 layer states, 109 tokens each) and then core.prefill_state_parity(model, ctx), which builds a NEW cache with 3 new layer states (70 tokens each). The first cache is freed in between. When CPython allocates a new layer state at the address of a freed one, raw[id(self)] still holds the 109 stale tokens of the dead object; the spy concatenates the new 70 tokens onto them and compares decoded() of the new object (n = 70) against canonical_state() of 179 tokens. The comparison fails although the canonical implementation is correct.
observer_bug.why_nondeterministic: whether a freed address is reused depends on the allocator state of the process
